Governments Back Global Agenda for More Competitive and Sustainable Air Transport Industry

Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 5:08
Instaread

Translations: Los gobiernos respaldan la “Agenda Global” para una industria de transporte aéreo más competitiva y sostenible (pdf) 

Les gouvernements appuient le programme mondial pour une industrie aérienne plus compétitive et durable (pdf)

(pdf) إياتا: الحكومات تتبنى أجندة عالمية لتعزيز تنافسية قطاع النقل الجوي واستدامته

国际航协：各国政府支持打造更具竞争力和可持续发展的航空运输业全球议程 (pdf)

Montreal – The International Air Transport Association (IATA) welcomed the successful conclusion of the 7th International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) Worldwide Air Transport Conference (ATConf/7). The agenda set out by governments supported key priorities for a more connected, competitive, sustainable and passenger-focused global air transport system.

ATConf/7 brought together ICAO Member States and industry stakeholders in Montreal, Canada, from 16–20 November under the theme, “Air Transport: Powering Global Connectivity, Economic Development and Resilience in a Dynamic World”.  The conference focused on priorities including economic regulation, consumer protection, infrastructure financing, innovation, resilience and sustainable growth, against a background of rising industry costs, capacity constraints, and fragmentary policies, particularly on sustainability.

As an official observer to ICAO, IATA submitted nine papers to the conference, including six Working Papers and three Information Papers. The submissions addressed economic regulation, consumer protection, airport and air navigation charges, sustainable aviation fuels (SAF), the Carbon Offsetting and Reduction Scheme for International Aviation (CORSIA), taxation, digital identity and passenger facilitation.

“The Worldwide Air Transport Conference has demonstrated the unique value of ICAO in bringing governments and industry together around global solutions for aviation. Globally, air transport supports 99 million jobs and generates $5 trillion in economic impact. Governments have sent a strong signal that those benefits can be maximized when regulation enables connectivity, competition and innovation rather than creating fragmentation and unnecessary cost. The challenge now is to turn the conference’s conclusions into action. A first order of business should be for EU member states to support the global CORSIA emissions initiative and prevent the cost and confusion of overlapping carbon programs which would result from the proposed expansion of the EU Emissions Trading System,” said Thomas Reynaert, IATA’s Senior Vice President for External Affairs.

Strong support for IATA priorities

 

Key outcomes aligned with priorities advanced by IATA included:

  • Smarter economic regulation: IATA urged governments to put connectivity, competitiveness and economic development at the heart of aviation regulation and proposed that ICAO develop practical regulatory practices, including the systematic use of impact assessments and cost-benefit analysis.
  • Effective consumer protection: Governments recognized the importance of approaches that protect passengers while maintaining choice and competition. IATA called for a focus on ensuring that travelers have access to clear and consistent information so that they have clear expectations about their air travel journey and understand both their rights and responsibilities.
  • Infrastructure costs and financing: The conference reinforced the importance of ICAO principles in the economic oversight of airports and air navigation service providers. IATA called for effective independent regulation based on cost-relatedness, transparency and meaningful consultation, ensuring that infrastructure investment responds efficiently to demand.
  • A stronger global approach to sustainability: IATA called for governments to move beyond SAF mandates and establish coordinated policies that stimulate production, investment and infrastructure while avoiding competitive distortions. It also urged governments to reinforce CORSIA as the single global market-based mechanism for international aviation emissions, including through increased availability of eligible emissions units and avoiding overlapping national or regional measures.
  • Seamless and secure travel: IATA and Airports Council International (ACI) highlighted the potential for globally interoperable digital identity to make travel simpler, more secure and efficient. IATA also pressed for consistent implementation of ICAO Annex 9, harmonized Advance Passenger Information (API) and Passenger Name Record (PNR) requirements, and clearer recognition that governments retain responsibility for decisions on passenger admissibility.
  • Globally consistent taxation: IATA and ACI urged governments to ensure that emerging international tax rules respect ICAO’s established framework for international aviation, protecting existing residence-based taxation arrangements and avoiding overlapping taxing rights, double taxation and unnecessary complexity.

ATConf/7 was the first worldwide ICAO Air Transport Conference since 2013, placing particular importance on setting policy direction against a significantly changed operating and economic environment. The sharp increase in fuel price and the general cost of living means that air passenger growth in 2026 will likely be the lowest since 2009 (excepting the pandemic years).

“Global standards have been one of aviation’s great strengths. With the temptation towards regulatory fragmentation growing, ATConf/7 reaffirmed the importance of governments working through ICAO. Airlines need regulation that is globally coherent, evidence-based and focused on delivering benefits for passengers. And air cargo is not simply a transport activity, but a critical component of global trade and connectivity that requires regulatory frameworks tailored to its unique operational requirements. In a period when air transport is under the greatest pressure it has seen since the pandemic, the discussions at this conference have been positive. IATA will work with ICAO and governments to maintain the momentum from Montreal,” said Reynaert.

See more on our engagement at the 7th ICAO Worldwide Air Transport Conference

Your Privacy

We process your data to deliver content or advertisements and measure the delivery of such content or advertisements to extract insights about our website. We share this information with our partners on the basis of consent. You may exercise your right to consent, based on a specific purpose below or at a partner level in the link under each purpose. Some vendors may process your data based on their legitimate interests, which does not require your consent. You cannot object to tracking technologies placed to ensure security, prevent fraud, fix errors, or deliver and present advertising and content, and precise geolocation data and active scanning of device characteristics for identification may be used to support this purpose. This exception does not apply to targeted advertising. These choices will be signaled to our vendors participating in the Transparency and Consent Framework. The choices you make regarding the purposes and vendors listed in this notice are saved and stored locally on your device for a maximum duration of 1 year.
Cookie Policy

Strictly Necessary Cookies

Always Active

These cookies are necessary for the website to function and cannot be switched off in our systems. They are usually only set in response to actions made by you which amount to a request for services, such as setting your privacy preferences, logging in or filling in forms. You can set your browser to block or alert you about these cookies, but some parts of the site will not then work. These cookies do not store any personally identifiable information.

Performance Cookies

These cookies allow us to count visits and traffic sources so we can measure and improve the performance of our site. They help us to know which pages are the most and least popular and see how visitors move around the site. All information these cookies collect is aggregated and therefore anonymous. If you do not allow these cookies we will not know when you have visited our site, and will not be able to monitor its performance.

Functional Cookies

These cookies enable the website to provide enhanced functionality and personalisation. They may be set by us or by third party providers whose services we have added to our pages. If you do not allow these cookies then some or all of these services may not function properly.

Targeting Cookies

These cookies may be set through our site by our advertising partners. They may be used by those companies to build a profile of your interests and show you relevant adverts on other sites. They do not store directly personal information, but are based on uniquely identifying your browser and internet device. If you do not allow these cookies, you will experience less targeted advertising.

Store and/or access information on a device 4 partners can use this purpose

Cookies, device or similar online identifiers (e.g. login-based identifiers, randomly assigned identifiers, network based identifiers) together with other information (e.g. browser type and information, language, screen size, supported technologies etc.) can be stored or read on your device to recognise it each time it connects to an app or to a website, for one or several of the purposes presented here.

Personalised advertising and content, advertising and content measurement, audience research and services development 4 partners can use this purpose

  • Use limited data to select advertising 4 partners can use this purpose

    Advertising presented to you on this service can be based on limited data, such as the website or app you are using, your non-precise location, your device type or which content you are (or have been) interacting with (for example, to limit the number of times an ad is presented to you).

  • Create profiles for personalised advertising 4 partners can use this purpose

    Information about your activity on this service (such as forms you submit, content you look at) can be stored and combined with other information about you (for example, information from your previous activity on this service and other websites or apps) or similar users. This is then used to build or improve a profile about you (that might include possible interests and personal aspects). Your profile can be used (also later) to present advertising that appears more relevant based on your possible interests by this and other entities.

  • Use profiles to select personalised advertising 4 partners can use this purpose

    Advertising presented to you on this service can be based on your advertising profiles, which can reflect your activity on this service or other websites or apps (like the forms you submit, content you look at), possible interests and personal aspects.

  • Measure advertising performance 4 partners can use this purpose

    Information regarding which advertising is presented to you and how you interact with it can be used to determine how well an advert has worked for you or other users and whether the goals of the advertising were reached. For instance, whether you saw an ad, whether you clicked on it, whether it led you to buy a product or visit a website, etc. This is very helpful to understand the relevance of advertising campaigns.

  • Understand audiences through statistics or combinations of data from different sources 3 partners can use this purpose

    Reports can be generated based on the combination of data sets (like user profiles, statistics, market research, analytics data) regarding your interactions and those of other users with advertising or (non-advertising) content to identify common characteristics (for instance, to determine which target audiences are more receptive to an ad campaign or to certain contents).

  • Develop and improve services 3 partners can use this purpose

    Information about your activity on this service, such as your interaction with ads or content, can be very helpful to improve products and services and to build new products and services based on user interactions, the type of audience, etc. This specific purpose does not include the development or improvement of user profiles and identifiers.

Use precise geolocation data 2 partners can use this special feature

With your acceptance, your precise location (within a radius of less than 500 metres) may be used in support of the purposes explained in this notice.

Ensure security, prevent and detect fraud, and fix errors 4 partners can use this special purpose

Always Active

Your data can be used to monitor for and prevent unusual and possibly fraudulent activity (for example, regarding advertising, ad clicks by bots), and ensure systems and processes work properly and securely. It can also be used to correct any problems you, the publisher or the advertiser may encounter in the delivery of content and ads and in your interaction with them.

Deliver and present advertising and content 4 partners can use this special purpose

Always Active

Certain information (like an IP address or device capabilities) is used to ensure the technical compatibility of the content or advertising, and to facilitate the transmission of the content or ad to your device.

Save and communicate privacy choices 3 partners can use this special purpose

Always Active

The choices you make regarding the purposes and entities listed in this notice are saved and made available to those entities in the form of digital signals (such as a string of characters). This is necessary in order to enable both this service and those entities to respect such choices.

Match and combine data from other data sources 3 partners can use this feature

Always Active

Information about your activity on this service may be matched and combined with other information relating to you and originating from various sources (for instance your activity on a separate online service, your use of a loyalty card in-store, or your answers to a survey), in support of the purposes explained in this notice.

Link different devices 2 partners can use this feature

Always Active

In support of the purposes explained in this notice, your device might be considered as likely linked to other devices that belong to you or your household (for instance because you are logged in to the same service on both your phone and your computer, or because you may use the same Internet connection on both devices).

Identify devices based on information transmitted automatically 3 partners can use this feature

Always Active

Your device might be distinguished from other devices based on information it automatically sends when accessing the Internet (for instance, the IP address of your Internet connection or the type of browser you are using) in support of the purposes exposed in this notice.
